decisions.decision: Database design gate CONFIRMED: two nullable TEXT columns (exterior_color, car_type) on vehicles, no DEFAULT, no CHECK, no new index, and the OR-semantics conditional UPDATE.
decisions.why: User confirmed the design, the per-query index justification (every access locates its row via the existing UNIQUE (account_id, tesla_id) index; neither column is ever a predicate), and the deliberate no-CHECK divergence from the access_type precedent (open-ended Tesla enums).

decisions.decision: Kept the uppercase change/folder name RM6-account-add-vehicle-config-fields despite the worker's report that the OpenSpec CLI rejects it.
decisions.why: Verified directly: `openspec validate --strict` (the gate the pipeline uses) ACCEPTS the uppercase name; only `new change` and `status --change` reject it, and neither is needed again. Archiving here is a manual domain-grouped git mv, so nothing downstream depends on the CLI. Matches the skill contract and the RM1-RM4 archive precedent.

decisions.decision: Leader-corrected four defects in the worker's artifacts before implementation rather than re-dispatching: (a) a doc comment falsely claiming the method never overwrites a captured value, (b) an unverified assertion about sqlc's inferred bind-param Go type, (c) a vague/skippable self-heal test, (d) a lowercase change name in T6.4.
decisions.why: All four are small factual corrections, not design changes; fixing them inline costs a fraction of a re-dispatch, and (a) and (c) would otherwise have been copied verbatim into the implementation and the test suite.
